ordered_diagnoses: Septic shock due to bacterial infection

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of hemodynamic shock and multi-organ dysfunction in a patient with a history of chromosome 18q deletion and well-controlled epilepsy
salient_findings: Hemodynamic shock requiring intubation and vasopressor support
Elevated troponin and brain natriuretic peptide levels
key_facts: Four days of fever prior to presentation
Mother was ill with a cough
Hemodynamic shock requiring intubation and vasopressor support
Elevated N-terminal brain natriuretic peptide level (9959 pg/mL)
Evidence of kidney injury, liver injury, and coagulopathy
Bilateral hazy opacities on chest radiographs
Moderately depressed biventricular function on echocardiogram (ejection fraction 42%)

shortlist: Septic shock due to bacterial infection

shortlist.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Low ADAMTS13 activity and elevated von Willebrand factor activity

shortlist.label: Viral myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin-I level and moderately depressed biventricular function

shortlist.label: Septic shock due to bacterial infection
shortlist.why_kept: Hemodynamic shock and evidence of multi-organ dysfunction

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Hemodynamic shock and mother's illness with a cough

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Evidence of kidney injury, liver injury, and coagulopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's low ADAMTS13 activity, elevated von Willebrand factor activity, and evidence of kidney injury, liver injury, and coagulopathy are consistent with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), a disorder characterized by the formation of blood clots in small blood vessels throughout the body.

rejected.label: Viral myocarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated troponin-I and N-terminal brain natriuretic peptide levels, the presence of low ADAMTS13 activity and elevated von Willebrand factor activity points more towards TTP than viral myocarditis

rejected.label: Septic shock due to bacterial infection
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a bacterial infection, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are more consistent with TTP

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of a streptococcal infection, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not align with this diagnosis

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: While the patient has evidence of kidney injury, liver injury, and coagulopathy, the specific laboratory findings such as low ADAMTS13 activity and elevated von Willebrand factor activity are more consistent with TTP
